description: Batch 4: regressions from the pre-release audit. Every case here is a measured bypass or a measured false positive from an out-of-corpus probe, not a hypothetical. N-* newline separation; I-012..I-020 interpreter identity and bundled short flags; I-021..I-022 the project's own build; O-006..O-008 download-and-execute chains.

cases.note: Measured bypass. Newline is a statement separator in both pwsh and bash; scanOperators did not cover it, so the whole chain reached the rules layer as a single token stream whose head was `echo`.
Same channel with a hard-rule payload on the second line. The deny must not be reachable only when the operator writes it on one line.
CRLF. Windows tooling emits this by default, so a newline rule that only knows LF is not a rule.
Backtick-n escape inside a nested shell. Already caught by the nested-shell rule, kept as a regression so the newline work cannot be traded for a hole here.
Control for the newline rule: a newline inside quotes is data, not a second statement. A naive `cmd.includes('\n')` would fail this.
Control: quoted git format string containing a literal newline escape. Same failure mode as N-005.
Measured bypass. `INTERPRETERS.has(head)` compared the whole first token, so a drive-qualified interpreter never matched and the inline body was never seen.
Measured bypass. Version suffix (`python3.11`, `node18`) is the documented way to pick an interpreter and broke exact matching.
Measured bypass on the POSIX side. Absolute interpreter path, same root cause as I-012.
Measured bypass: version-suffixed node with an inline body.
Control for the identity fix: normalising the interpreter must not make a workspace-relative script fail. Path provenance still says pass.
Measured bypass. `-uc` is unbuffered plus `-c`; INLINE_FLAGS was an exact-match set, so bundled short flags read as an ordinary script call.
Measured bypass. `-pe` is print plus eval, the documented one-liner form.
Measured bypass. Bundled flags in the other order; a fix that only checks for a leading `-c` would miss it.
Both fixes at once: qualified interpreter and a volatile target. Either one alone should be enough.
Measured false positive: this project's own build asked for approval on every run, which trains the operator to click through. A local compiler is not a fetch-and-execute.
Same toolchain allowlist, flag-only form.
The allowlist must not become a chain bypass: the split layer still sees the chain before interp does.
Measured bypass. Classic download-and-execute one-liner. The payload is not in the command, and nothing in the earlier layers objected.
Measured bypass. certutil as a downloader, a documented living-off-the-land technique.
Decode to executable: the real payload never appears as readable text in the command.
Control: certutil used for hashing, which is the legitimate reason it ships. Only the download and decode verbs are signals.
